title: Professional hems: choose, level and sew them right

say: Professional hems: choose, level and sew them right.
This is the video for module one of Fashion Finishing and Quality Control.

The hem is the first thing a client sees when a garment moves. A good hem does three jobs: it stops fraying, adds a little weight so the garment hangs well, and gives a clean line the eye reads as quality.

panel.heading: The hem is what a client sees first
items: Stops the edge fraying
Adds weight so it hangs well
Gives a clean line that reads as quality
A poor hem looks homemade

say: A wavy, uneven hem, or one showing stitches where it should not, makes even beautiful fabric look homemade.

items: Stops the edge fraying

say: Choose a hem by fabric weight, edge shape, formality and quantity. A straight hem can take a deep allowance, because the fold is the same length as the garment it lies against. Straight trousers take about 3 to 5 cm.

panel.heading: The more curved the edge, the narrower
items: Straight trousers, pencil skirts: 3 to 5 cm
Gently A-line: 2 to 3 cm, ease the fullness
Full circle skirts: 1 cm or less
Curved shirt-tail: 0.6 to 1 cm double fold

say: On a curved edge, the raw edge is longer than the place it folds up to, so a deep hem ripples. A gentle A-line takes about 2 to 3 cm.

panel.heading: The more curved the edge, the narrower
items: Straight trousers, pencil skirts: 3 to 5 cm
Gently A-line: 2 to 3 cm, ease the fullness
Full circle skirts: 1 cm or less
Curved shirt-tail: 0.6 to 1 cm double fold

say: A full circle skirt needs 1 cm or less, as a narrow fold, a rolled hem, or a facing. A curved shirt-tail takes a narrow double fold of about 0.6 to 1 cm.

say: For example, Kemi in Ibadan has three orders in one week. Navy crepe office trousers are formal and straight, so she uses an invisible hand blind hem with a 4 cm allowance.

panel.heading: Kemi's three orders, three hems

cards.d: Formal and straight: a hand blind hem with a 4 cm allowance, edge overlocked first.
Sheer and light: a narrow rolled hem with the rolled hem foot, about 3 mm finished.
Hang it 24 hours, level it, then a narrow double fold, topstitched.

say: A chiffon blouse cannot hold the weight of a deep fold, so it gets a narrow rolled hem, about 3 mm.

panel.heading: Kemi's three orders, three hems

cards.d: Formal and straight: a hand blind hem with a 4 cm allowance, edge overlocked first.
Sheer and light: a narrow rolled hem with the rolled hem foot, about 3 mm finished.
Hang it 24 hours, level it, then a narrow double fold, topstitched.

say: Her ankara circle skirt is cut partly on the bias, which stretches under its own weight. She hangs it for at least 24 hours before levelling. If she hemmed it at once, it would dip unevenly a week later.

panel.heading: Kemi's three orders, three hems

cards.d: Formal and straight: a hand blind hem with a 4 cm allowance, edge overlocked first.
Sheer and light: a narrow rolled hem with the rolled hem foot, about 3 mm finished.
Hang it 24 hours, level it, then a narrow double fold, topstitched.

say: Most crooked hems are not badly stitched. They were badly marked. Bodies are not symmetrical, and shoes change everything. So ask the client to wear the garment and the exact shoes, and stand naturally.

panel.heading: Mark the hem up from the floor
items: Client wears the garment and her shoes
Agree the length at the front first
Same floor measurement all round
Check side seams hang straight
Lay flat and true the line
panel.rule: Never measure down from the waist. Measure up from the floor.

say: Agree the length at the front, measure it from the floor with an upright ruler, and use that same measurement all round. Pin every 5 to 8 cm, moving yourself around her.

panel.heading: Mark the hem up from the floor
items: Client wears the garment and her shoes
Agree the length at the front first
Same floor measurement all round
Check side seams hang straight
Lay flat and true the line
panel.rule: Never measure down from the waist. Measure up from the floor.

say: If a side seam swings, fix the fit first. A hem cannot hide a fitting problem. Then lay the garment flat and true the pins into a smooth line.

say: Finish the raw edge by overlocking or zigzag. Press the fold only, and tack it.

panel.heading: Invisible from the right side
items: Finish the raw edge, press the fold
Fold the edge back about 0.5 cm
Catch 1 or 2 threads of the garment
Move 0.8 to 1 cm, stitch the allowance
Keep thread relaxed; check every 10 cm

say: Use a fine needle and a single strand of matching thread, about 50 cm long. Fold the hem edge back about 0.5 cm, and pick up only one or two threads from the garment layer.

panel.heading: Invisible from the right side
items: Finish the raw edge, press the fold
Fold the edge back about 0.5 cm
Catch 1 or 2 threads of the garment
Move 0.8 to 1 cm, stitch the allowance
Keep thread relaxed; check every 10 cm
panel.rule: Catch only 1 or 2 threads of the outer fabric.

say: Move along about 0.8 to 1 cm and take a small stitch in the allowance. Keep the thread relaxed, because tight thread pulls dimples. Every 10 cm, turn it over and check the right side.

panel.heading: Invisible from the right side
items: Finish the raw edge, press the fold
Fold the edge back about 0.5 cm
Catch 1 or 2 threads of the garment
Move 0.8 to 1 cm, stitch the allowance
Keep thread relaxed; check every 10 cm
panel.rule: Catch only 1 or 2 threads of the outer fabric.

say: For batch orders, machine hems can look just as professional. For example, Halima in Kano has 24 aso-ebi skirts, each hem about 180 cm round. By hand, each takes 30 minutes, which is 12 hours in all.

panel.heading: Halima's 24 skirts: hand or machine?
items: By hand: 30 minutes per skirt
24 skirts x 30 minutes = 12 hours
Machine blind hem: about 8 minutes
24 x 8 = 192 minutes, about 3 hours
Saved: 528 minutes, almost 9 hours

say: With a machine blind hem foot, the side bite just catches the fold. One skirt takes about 8 minutes. 24 skirts take about 3 hours.

panel.heading: Halima's 24 skirts: hand or machine?

say: She saves almost 9 working hours. For knits, use a twin needle or overlocker, so the hem can stretch without snapping.

say: Press from the wrong side with a press cloth. Lower the iron, press, lift and move. Sliding stretches the hem.

panel.heading: Press it right, press it safely

cards.d: Wrong side, press cloth. Lower, press, lift. Do not slide the iron or it stretches.
Slip brown paper under the allowance. Test heat on a scrap first.
Iron on its heel, never left on, cord out of walkways and away from children. Unplug after.

say: Slip a strip of brown paper between the allowance and the garment, so no ridge shows. Dark crepe and polyester shine easily, so test heat on a scrap first.

panel.heading: Press it right, press it safely

cards.d: Wrong side, press cloth. Lower, press, lift. Do not slide the iron or it stretches.
Slip brown paper under the allowance. Test heat on a scrap first.
Iron on its heel, never left on, cord out of walkways and away from children. Unplug after.

say: Keep the iron on its heel, never leave it on when you step away, and keep the cord away from walkways and children. Unplug it at the end of the session.

say: To remember. Curved edges need narrow hems. Hang bias and circle skirts for 24 hours. Mark up from the floor, with the client in her shoes. A blind hem catches only one or two threads. And test every machine setting on a scrap of the real fabric.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Curved edges need narrow hems
Hang bias and circle skirts 24 hours
Mark up from the floor, in her shoes
Blind hem: catch 1 or 2 threads only
Test every machine setting on scrap
